title: String concatenation
instruction: Concatenate first_name and last_name with a space, print it.
starter_code:
first_name = "Ada"
last_name = "Lovelace"
# Create full_name and print it
solution_code:
first_name = "Ada"
last_name = "Lovelace"
full_name = first_name + " " + last_name
print(full_name)
test_suite:
import io, sys
import re

def t1():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == "Ada Lovelace\n"

title: Use an f-string
instruction: Use an f-string to print the population info for Tokyo.
starter_code:
city = "Tokyo"
population = 37_000_000
# Print using an f-string
solution_code:
city = "Tokyo"
population = 37_000_000
print(f"{city} has a population of {population}.")
test_suite:
import io, sys
import re

def t1():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()

title: Check string length
instruction: Print the length of quote, then whether **mind** is in it.
starter_code:
quote = "The mind is everything. What you think you become."
# Print length, then check if "mind" is in quote
solution_code:
quote = "The mind is everything. What you think you become."
print(len(quote))
print("mind" in quote)
test_suite:
import io, sys
import re

def t1():
    captured = io.StringIO()
    sys.stdout = captured
    exec(open("exercise.py").read())
    sys.stdout = sys.__stdout__
    output = captured.getvalue()
    assert output == "50\nTrue\n"
